## Prototype approval, before any bench work below

Do not skip straight from a KiCad save to the bench procedures below. `manufacturing/release_guard.py --route prototype` checks a separate, fixed decision (`design/release-gates.json`'s `decisions.prototype`) that must be satisfied and explicitly approved by a human -- reviewed power/pin design, actual footprint mapping, completed layout plus native ERC/DRC/parity, the assembler's DFM review, and a controlled current-limited/staged-enable bring-up plan -- before ordering the assembled board this page's procedures run on. That decision never reads or requires G01/G02/G03/G04/G05/G06/G07/G08/G09/G10's CLOSED status, and it never claims any bench result from this page in advance. See `LOCAL-HANDOFF.md`'s "Prototype approval" section for the exact prerequisite list.

## Before the populated board is powered

Ask the assembler or bench-service provider to check component identity, numeric pin mapping, solder joints, shorts, module orientation, power/header continuity and the exact approved module revision. Confirm F1 and USB source current path. Use a current-limited 5 V source. Note that the display backlight is default ON at power-up (it is active-low on GP13 through the carrier's Q1 open-drain stage, #41) and goes dark only once firmware drives GP13 high; the LCD-off build does that from its early init hook. Capture the GP13/gate/`LCD_BL` waveforms per `design/evidence/backlight-interface.md` before G01/G06 closure. Rework belongs to that provider, not the home workstation.

Power tests first establish analog/digital rails, 3.0 V reference, startup/off decay, USB current and absence of back-power. Measure current separately with no display, dark display and bright display. Obtain board/module thermal images or measured hot-spot temperatures under worst intended load.

## Channel tests

Use a verified low-voltage signal fixture with the same ground and appropriate current limits. Begin with inputs shorted to ground, then step through measured ±1, ±3, ±5, ±8 and ±12 V. Record raw codes and DMM readings for all ten channels. Verify expected open-input bias rather than treating it as a defect or auto-zeroing it away. Test all TIME endpoints/direction and all three RANGE positions.

After normal-range DC validation, check 1 Hz, 10 Hz, 100 Hz, 500 Hz and 1 kHz signals, then deliberately characterize aliasing above the intended range. Compare displayed amplitude against reference instrumentation and the predicted filter transfer function. Distinguish source distortion from this monitor's filtering, conversion and display effects.

Worst-case mux test: alternate a near-positive-full-scale channel and a near-negative-full-scale channel, hold neighboring channels at zero, and measure residual settling/crosstalk with the LCD off and active. Increase rate only while recording discarded/kept conversion timing and overrun counts. An 8 µs slot is acceptable only when its measured error meets the reviewed target.

## Separate abnormal-voltage qualification

Do not apply ±24 V merely because the design spreadsheet contains it. First review all clamp paths and absolute maximum constraints, then conduct a controlled powered/unpowered current-limited test at a suitably equipped provider. Inspect both source and internal node currents and any back-powered rail. ESD immunity is a separate test; successful DC injection is not an IEC ESD claim.

## Initial proposed acceptance limits

These are engineering targets, not achieved results. Review them after the first measured sample:

| Item | Proposed target |
|---|---|
| Calibrated DC residual, low-impedance source | no more than 100 mV over ±8 V, excluding noise outliers |
| Channel crosstalk on DC steps | no more than 100 mV input-referred after the selected settling interval |
| Reliable useful bandwidth | characterize DC–1 kHz amplitude error; do not assume flatness |
| High-rate acquisition | ten actual 10 ksample/s streams with counted overruns and measured skew |
| RANGE state | stable reading after 20 ms; no indefinite intermediate-state oscillation |
| LCD behavior | all ten panes, correct orientation/colors/labels; readable physical-scale text |
| User assembly | no unsoldered electrical part or wire after delivery |

No hardware result is prefilled in `manufacturing/acceptance-results.csv`. Failed items remain visible. The first populated prototype may require a second PCB revision; do not shift that rework onto the user.
